arc.note: Minimum weeks, assuming every gate passes first time. Phases advance on measurements, not dates, so the real number is longer -- a repeated rung or a held gate costs weeks, and that is the plan working rather than failing.

bone_window.note: Bone adapts months behind the fitness that lets you run further, and appears in none of the heart-rate measures. For the first 20 weeks of running, single runs are capped against your own recent longest: prefer more frequent, shorter runs over one long one, vary the surface, and treat focal bone pain as a stop rather than a niggle.

gates.label: 42+ km/week for three consecutive weeks
gates.rationale: The base a marathon block is built on. Going into marathon-specific work below this is the single most common reason first marathons go badly.

gates.label: 10K completed
gates.rationale: The first legitimate Riegel input. Below 10K the extrapolation to marathon distance spans too large a distance ratio to mean much, which is why no marathon prediction appears before this.

gates.label: Half marathon completed
gates.rationale: The best available predictor of marathon readiness, and a rehearsal of fuelling, pacing and kit at a distance where mistakes are survivable.

gates.label: No pain above 2/10 for two weeks
gates.rationale: The pain-monitoring model treats 0-2/10 as acceptable, 3-5/10 as a warning to hold volume, and anything above 5/10 as a stop. Two clean weeks means the tissue is tolerating the current load, which is the precondition for adding more.

gates.label: 80% of planned sessions completed over 4 weeks
gates.rationale: Consistency is the variable that actually predicts progress. Advancing a phase on the strength of a good fortnight inside a patchy block just moves the problem forward.

outline.goal: Build the long run and race a half marathon.
outline.label: Half Build

gates.label: Three long runs of 26 km or more
gates.rationale: Time on feet is the specific adaptation the marathon demands, and one long run does not build it.

gates.label: Long-run decoupling under 6%
gates.rationale: Aerobic durability at duration -- the thing that decides whether the last 10 km is running or survival.

gates.label: 48+ km/week for three consecutive weeks
gates.rationale: Peak-phase volume floor for a 3-day-a-week schedule with cross-training.

gates.label: No pain above 2/10 for two weeks
gates.rationale: The pain-monitoring model treats 0-2/10 as acceptable, 3-5/10 as a warning to hold volume, and anything above 5/10 as a stop. Two clean weeks means the tissue is tolerating the current load, which is the precondition for adding more.

gates.label: 80% of planned sessions completed over 4 weeks
gates.rationale: Consistency is the variable that actually predicts progress. Advancing a phase on the strength of a good fortnight inside a patchy block just moves the problem forward.

outline.goal: Develop marathon-specific endurance: the long run is the point.
outline.label: Marathon Base

gates.label: Two long runs with marathon-pace segments
gates.rationale: Rehearses race pace on tired legs, which is the only way to know it is realistic.

gates.label: A long run of 150+ minutes
gates.rationale: Time on feet matters more than distance for a first marathon.

gates.label: Race fuelling rehearsed on two long runs
gates.rationale: The gut is trainable and untrained guts fail at 30 km. Practise the exact products and timing you will use.

gates.label: No pain above 2/10 for two weeks
gates.rationale: The pain-monitoring model treats 0-2/10 as acceptable, 3-5/10 as a warning to hold volume, and anything above 5/10 as a stop. Two clean weeks means the tissue is tolerating the current load, which is the precondition for adding more.

outline.goal: Rehearse race day -- marathon pace, fuelling, and the long run at size.
outline.label: Marathon Peak

outline.goal: Cut volume, keep intensity, arrive fresh.
outline.label: Taper

weeks.focus: Make running a habit and finish a 5K. Volume, not speed.
notes: Daniels would cap the long run at 30% of weekly volume at this level; this one is 35%. Three runs a week leaves no other way to build a marathon long run, so this is a real and accepted trade-off rather than an oversight -- and the time cap is what keeps it bounded.
No threshold work yet. Volume and consistency first -- threshold work on a thin base produces fatigue without much adaptation.

A fourth, short easy run is scheduled on Tuesday -- its distance comes out of the other two easy runs' share, not on top of it. Turn PlanConfig.offer_fourth_run off to go back to three runs a week; no gate depends on it.

ramp_protocol.at_each_stage: Say a full sentence out loud. Comfortable, effortful, or impossible?

steps.label: Walk warm-up
steps.say: Five minutes easy walking. Four and a half kilometres an hour.

steps.label: Steady block
steps.say: Twenty minutes at the fastest speed you could still talk comfortably.

steps.label: Cool down
steps.say: Five minutes walking to cool down.

stop_when_any: Heart rate reaches 169 bpm (85% of heart-rate reserve)
